column1: # Coastlines, as closed outlines in lon,lat degrees.
# Why outlines and not a grid of characters. The world is 72x36 hexes, which is
# 2592 cells, and a hand-corrected character grid of that size is not something
# a reviewer can check by reading. An outline is: a vertex is a place, you can
# see that it is wrong, and you can move it. scripts/gen_game_data.py rasterises
# these into the hex grid and asserts that all 70 ports end up reachable from
# one another by sea, so a coastline that walls a port in fails the build rather
# These are hand-placed from ordinary geographic knowledge at roughly 5-degree
# fidelity, which is the granularity the port coordinates come in. They are not
# derived from any dataset, so there is no licence to carry and no geospatial
# dependency to install. They are deliberately coarse: this is a chart, not a
# survey, and at one hex per 5 degrees the Baltic is two cells wide.
# Winding does not matter; the rasteriser uses an even-odd crossing test.
# Inland seas, carved out of the land above. A leading "-" subtracts.
# These exist because the source's port coordinates are stylised, not surveyed:
# it places Azov at N55 E30 and Trebizond at N45 E30, which on a real atlas is
# Belarus and Ukraine, and it puts Baghdad at N30 E50, which is open Gulf. The
# map has to match the game's geography rather than the world's, so the water
# is cut to reach the ports the data actually names.
